title: Adjectives: Describing People and Things
summary: Use adjectives to describe people and things. Put them before nouns or after be and verbs such as look, feel, smell, taste and sound.
learningObjectives: Place an adjective before the noun it describes.
Keep adjectives in the same form with singular and plural nouns.
Use adjectives after forms of be to describe a subject.
Use an adjective after look, feel, smell, taste and sound when describing the subject.

explanation.heading: An adjective describes a noun
explanation.body: Adjectives give information about people, places and things: size, colour, condition or opinion. When an adjective goes with a noun, it usually comes before that noun. It can follow a or an and other determiners.
explanation.example: We found a quiet café near the river.

explanation.heading: Adjectives do not change for plural nouns
explanation.body: Use the same adjective with one item or several items. Do not add -s to an adjective because the noun is plural: one empty box and three empty boxes.

explanation.heading: Put adjectives after be
explanation.body: An adjective can describe the subject after am, is, are, was or were. In this pattern, you do not need to put a noun after the adjective. For example, the room is warm, and the guests are happy.
explanation.example: The seats were comfortable on the long journey.

explanation.heading: Use adjectives after look and feel
explanation.body: After look and feel, use an adjective to describe how somebody or something seems or feels. These verbs connect the subject to its description; they do not tell us how someone performs an action.
explanation.example: You look relaxed, and I feel calm.

explanation.heading: Use adjectives after sound, smell and taste
explanation.body: Sound, smell and taste can also introduce a description of the subject. Say the music sounds beautiful, the flowers smell lovely and the fruit tastes sweet. The adjective describes the music, flowers or fruit.
explanation.example: That plan sounds sensible to me.

comparisons.title: Before a noun or after be

left.label: Before a noun
left.note: Soft comes before the noun blanket.

right.label: After be
right.note: Soft describes the subject after is.

comparisons.title: A description with a linking verb

right.label: Smell + adjective
right.note: Fresh describes the smell of the garden.

examples.sentence: The bakery sells warm bread every morning.
examples.note: Warm is an adjective before the noun bread.
Heavy does not change when the noun is plural.

examples.sentence: The meeting room is quiet today.
examples.note: Quiet describes a subject after is.

examples.sentence: My cousin looks tired after work.
examples.note: Tired describes how my cousin appears.
Sour describes the taste after tastes.

commonMistakes.why: An adjective normally comes before the noun it describes.
The adjective heavy stays unchanged before the plural noun bags.
An adjective does not take -s for a plural subject.
After smells, use an adjective to describe the perfume.

studyTips: Practise each adjective in two positions: a quiet room / the room is quiet.
Remember that a plural noun does not change an adjective: a clean plate / clean plates.
With look, feel, sound, smell and taste, ask what is being described. If it is the subject, use an adjective.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct description: We stayed in a ___ hotel.
exercises.feedback: Comfortable is an adjective; it describes the noun hotel.

exercises.prompt: Choose the word that completes the sentence: The fresh bread smells ___.
exercises.feedback: After smells, use the adjective wonderful to describe the bread.
Busy is an adjective after are. It has no plural -s or adverb ending.

exercises.prompt: Choose the word that completes the sentence: We saw three ___ birds in the garden.
exercises.feedback: Colourful is an adjective that describes the plural noun birds; its form stays the same.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the adjective 'bright': The kitchen is ___ in the morning.
exercises.feedback: An adjective can follow is to describe the kitchen.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the adjective 'green': There are two ___ bicycles outside.
exercises.feedback: Green comes before the plural noun bicycles and does not take -s.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the adjective 'tired': I feel ___ after the long walk.
exercises.feedback: Feel is followed by an adjective describing the speaker.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the adjective 'interesting': Your story sounds ___.
exercises.feedback: Sounds connects the subject, your story, to its description.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We live in a house large.
acceptedAnswers: We live in a large house.
exercises.feedback: The adjective large belongs before the noun house.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Their winter coats are reds.
exercises.feedback: Red stays the same after are, even with plural coats.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The soup tastes deliciously.
exercises.feedback: Tastes takes an adjective when it describes the soup.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Our new manager is patiently.
exercises.feedback: Use the adjective patient after is; patiently is an adverb.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say the corrected complete sentence: 'They have two blues bags.'
speakingExercises.feedback: Blue is an adjective and has no plural -s.

speakingExercises.prompt: Complete the sentence aloud using the adjective 'comfortable': 'That chair looks ___.'
speakingExercises.feedback: Looks links the chair to the adjective comfortable.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make a complete sentence in this order: 'a / friendly / neighbour / We / have'.
speakingExercises.feedback: Friendly is an adjective placed before neighbour.

speakingExercises.prompt: Three puppies are playful. Say one complete sentence beginning 'The three puppies' and ending 'are playful'.
speakingExercises.feedback: Playful is an adjective after are. Its form does not change for a plural subject.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change 'The room is very quiet' to a sentence beginning 'It is a' and ending 'room'. Keep 'very quiet'.
acceptedAnswers: It is a very quiet room.
speakingExercises.feedback: The adjective phrase very quiet comes before the noun room when you use it as a noun description.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks how the tea tastes. It is bitter. Reply with one sentence beginning 'The tea' and using 'tastes'.
speakingExercises.feedback: After tastes, the adjective bitter describes the tea, not an action.

speakingExercises.prompt: Someone says, 'The new pillows feel softly.' Correct the last word and say the whole sentence.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use the adjective soft after feel when it describes the pillows.

speakingExercises.prompt: Your new backpack is light and looks strong. Say exactly two short sentences. Begin the first with 'My backpack is' and the second with 'It looks'.
acceptedAnswers: My backpack is light. It looks strong.
speakingExercises.feedback: Light follows is, and strong follows looks; both adjectives describe the backpack.

listeningExercises.feedback: Light is the adjective you hear after are; it describes the trainers.

listeningExercises.prompt: Which word follows smells in the recording?
listeningExercises.feedback: Fresh is the adjective heard after the linking verb smells.

listeningExercises.audioText: The plates are clean and ready to use.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the adjective you hear immediately after are.
listeningExercises.feedback: Clean describes the plates after are.

listeningExercises.audioText: The little boy looked afraid when the big dog barked.
listeningExercises.prompt: How did the boy seem to feel?
listeningExercises.feedback: Looked afraid means he seemed scared; afraid describes the boy's feeling.

listeningExercises.audioText: The blue container on the top shelf is empty, but the green container below is full.
choices: The one on the top shelf
The one on the lower shelf
listeningExercises.feedback: The lower container is full, while the one above it is empty.

listeningExercises.audioText: The flowers smell lovely, but the old milk smells bad.
listeningExercises.prompt: What is different about the two smells?
listeningExercises.feedback: The flowers have a pleasant smell; the old milk does not. Lovely and bad are adjectives after smell.

listeningExercises.audioText: We sat in a quiet corner at the busy airport.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the adjective you hear immediately before 'corner'.
listeningExercises.feedback: Quiet describes the corner and comes before the noun.

listeningExercises.audioText: My neighbour's garden looks beautiful in spring.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the describing word you hear immediately after 'looks'.
listeningExercises.feedback: Beautiful describes the garden after the linking verb looks.
